newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Popocatepetl rains ash, rock in Puebla.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Popocatepetl rains ash, rock in Puebla.

text.p: Mexico's giant Popocatepetl volcano hurled ash and earth on neighbouring areas in a spurt of midday activity on Tuesday, local authorities said.

The sudden burst began at 1:07 p.m. (1807 GMT) and continued for nearly 15 minutes, sending a plume of ash about 9,842 feet (3,000 meters) in the air, the National Disaster Prevention Centre (Cenapred) said in a report.
Ash sprinkled on neighbouring towns of Cholula, Chipilo, San Jeronimo Tecuampan, Atlixco and San Pedro Benito Juarez in the state of Puebla, about 50 miles (80 km) east of Mexico City.
Residents in nearby towns ran for cover, some wearing face masks.

The 17,887-foot (5,465-meter) volcano has been blowing out ash and rock intermittently for the past month. Residents in the city of Puebla, one of Mexico's largest population centres, have been put on alert but not evacuated, officials said.
